data.title: Box Model
data.tagline: The box model is the browser's rule for the space used by an element's content, padding, border, and margin.
data.learningOutcome: You can inspect an element's content, padding, border, and margin and explain why its actual footprint differs from expectation.
data.description: A card with 320px of content width can occupy more after horizontal padding and a border, leaving two columns unable to fit. A button's hit area is affected by these layers too. The box model explains size calculation, not whether excess content should show, clip, or scroll.

learning.assumes: You have adjusted a card's width, padding, or border.
learning.outcome: You can inspect an element's content, padding, border, and margin and explain why its actual footprint differs from expectation.

explanation.title: Content is not the whole width
explanation.text: The content box holds text and images; padding creates breathing room, border wraps them, and margin separates the element from its neighbors.

explanation.title: Layout uses the actual footprint
explanation.text: When elements sit side by side, the browser calculates the space they truly occupy. DevTools box-model inspection shows whether content, padding, border, or margin caused the squeeze.

data.boundary: The box model is not Flex or Grid. Flex and Grid arrange multiple elements; the box model determines the footprint of each element. Overflow decides what happens when there is not enough space.

lessonPractice.title: Two cards each use `width: 50%` and each add 24px left and right padding, then overflow horizontally. What concept should you inspect first?

options.label: Inspect whether width must also account for padding and border in the box model, then choose the sizing rule
options.feedback: Correct. A card's actual space may exceed its content width, so inspecting its layers best explains why two columns no longer fit.

options.label: Inspect the search keyword because card text may be too long
options.feedback: Text length can create another issue, but the shared change here is the padding added to every card.

options.label: Inspect cross-origin settings because layout failures are usually CORS
options.feedback: CORS governs cross-origin reads, not CSS size calculation.

data.agentPrompt: Inspect the box model of these two-column cards and state the space used by content width, padding, border, and margin. Keep two columns on desktop and prevent horizontal overflow at 390px; afterward confirm the computed size in developer tools.
